name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy; flindersandoutback.com.au/towns/coober-pedy; southaustralia.com Flinders Ranges and Outback
name_evidence.wording: opal-mining town with underground dugouts, the outback's main tourist stop on the Stuart Highway

new_destinations.note: The town is the destination, not a spot of itself. Moon Plain (~15 km per source) and Breakaways (~33 km north) sit inside 75% of span. Needs checking: Moon Plain point.

new_destinations.name: Innamincka

name_evidence.wording: remote Cooper Creek township, Burke and Wills country, gateway to Innamincka Regional Reserve and Coongie Lakes

new_destinations.note: Exactly four spots; Coongie Lakes is the farthest, span set from it after the pin stage (shrink to 60 if it lands inside 45 km of centre; if Coongie fails the 75% test it goes standalone and Innamincka reverts to standalone town + spots).

places.reason: Wikivoyage See listing: self-guided tour of a 1916 mine and underground homes, a signature Coober Pedy visit (rule 2)

places.name: Tom's Working Opal Mine

review.name: Painted Desert (South Australia)
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage names it, SA Heritage lists the Arckaringa Hills state heritage area, and Arckaringa Station offers a walk (~1.5 km) and lookout at sunset; distinct natural sight. Against: only one counted source (Wikivoyage Stuart Highway, 'all-wheel track'), sits on a private pastoral lease with restricted, fragile access, 120-150 km from Coober Pedy; no tourism-board page found.

review.name: Catholic Catacomb Church
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy calls the underground Catholic church 'a significant site' and Coober Pedy's carved-rock churches are a signature visit. Against: Wikivoyage ranks it less intricate than the Serbian Orthodox church; one counted source; the candidate's wiki title (Catacomb Church) is actually the Anglican church, so name and article conflict and the Catholic church's identity needs checking.

review.name: Marree Man
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Marree See entry and Flinders & Outback both name it; a famous 4.2 km geoglyph. Against: it cannot be seen from the ground and the experience is a charter flight from Marree (an operator), so a visitor 'goes' to nothing; only the flight reaches it.

review.name: Kalamurina Sanctuary
review.reason: For: AWC (the manager) describes a 679,000 ha wildlife sanctuary on the Warburton River with an interpretive walk on Outback Spirit pre-booked tours (April-October). Against: no tourism-board or guide source; third-party listings say camping is closed and entry is tours only, and AWC's own page allows booked self-drive at $40 per vehicle, so access sources conflict.

standalone_near_destination_40km: none: every kept place within 40 km of Coober Pedy (Breakaways, Moon Plain, Big Winch, golf) is a spot of it; nothing within 40 km of Innamincka outside it.

why_not_destinations.Oodnadatta Track: a 617 km linear route named by Wikivoyage; its stops are 100-300 km apart with no common base, so standalone spots, with the track pinned at its route midpoint
why_not_destinations.Woomera / Roxby Downs / Andamooka: two or three spots each, 90+ km apart: standalone
why_not_destinations.Witjira National Park: park with only Dalhousie Springs beside it: two spots, below the four-spot bar and not rank 1-2; standalone (Dalhousie sits inside the park, kept as its own place per the judge)
why_not_destinations.Kati Thanda-Lake Eyre / Munga-Thirri-Sim: single-park places with no kept walks or villages; below the four-spot bar; standalone

notes: Birdsville and Oodnadatta Tracks placed here per run-wide decision; coordinates null until the route midpoint is resolved.
Marree town kept beside Marree Mosque: the town is the hub for two tracks and has the Marree Man access (review), not just the mosque; flag for owner.
